contracts.commit_point: The await run_agent(...) call in the /chat handler at agent/server.py:647-652, which begins agent execution via runner.run_async at agent/server.py:413-417 and commits the external Google API requests; the inline wait must complete and _last_request_time must be updated (line 630) before this commit point is reached.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Module-level global timestamp throttle: _last_request_time and _MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL = 2.0 are declared for the Google API to avoid 429 errors (agent/server.py:147-150); chat() enforces it inline by computing time_since_last, awaiting asyncio.sleep(wait_time) when time_since_last < _MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL, and then updating _last_request_time = time.time() (agent/server.py:624-630) before run_agent is called.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Invoking the agent from the /chat handler (run_agent, which drives runner.run_async and the outbound Google API model calls) when less than _MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL (2.0 seconds) have elapsed since _last_request_time was recorded, i.e., agent invocations more frequent than once per 2 seconds that would trigger Google API rate-limit (429) errors.
pending_binding_information: Whether the obligation is intended to bind to an agent-mediated dispatch path (agent tool or lifecycle hook) or remains scoped to the HTTP /chat handler only.

contracts.protected_operation: Invocation of the Google Gemini-backed agent from the POST /chat handler: chat() awaits run_agent(user_id, session_id, message, memory_context), which executes runner.run_async and produces external Google API model requests.
contracts.protected_resource: External Google Gemini/LLM API rate-limit quota (the Google API named as the rate-limit target at agent/server.py:147 and 624).
contracts.protection_obligation: Chat requests submitted to POST /chat must be throttled to a minimum interval of 2.0 seconds before the Google Gemini-backed agent is invoked via run_agent, so that the agent is never invoked more than once per 2 seconds and back-to-back invocations do not exhaust the external Google API quota (429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED). scope_limits: The throttle is evidenced only inside the POST /chat handler; the supplied source shows no equivalent wait in the /api/voice/chat handler, which also invokes run_agent (agent/server.py:1833-1838), and no throttle is shown for scheduler-driven agent runs.

The mechanism is a single process-global timestamp, not per-user or distributed; because asyncio.sleep yields before _last_request_time is updated, concurrent requests can each pass the check after their own sleeps, so the source does not establish strict serial pacing under concurrency.
The guard delays requests (awaits) rather than rejecting them; it bounds request pacing toward the Google API and does not itself enforce or track a quota.

The guard is wired to an HTTP endpoint handler; no agent tool registration, lifecycle hook, or agent-generated-input dataflow binds this operation to agent mediation, so agent_mediation is recorded as not_established and no agent_entry_binding evidence is cited.

missing_information: No supplied source view shows a decorator, registration, callback wiring, tool dispatch, or concrete dataflow binding the throttled agent invocation to agent mediation (agent tool, lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input reaching the guarded effect); agent_mediation is therefore not_established.
No supplied source shows the throttle applied to any path other than POST /chat; coverage of /api/voice/chat and scheduler-driven agent runs is unverified.
Concurrency and race behavior of _last_request_time under simultaneous requests is not addressed in the supplied source.
